changes.explanation: Susceptibility to local anaesthetic runs opposite to fibre size, so the small B, C and A-delta fibres are generally blocked before larger A fibres. That gradient is what allows a local anaesthetic to abolish pain while touch, pressure and motor power are still present. The distractors are wrong because velocity is directly rather than inversely proportional to diameter, A-delta fibres are sensory and carry fast sharp pain rather than somatic motor commands, and A-alpha fibres include sensory proprioceptive afferents as well as motor efferents.

evidence.claim: B fibers usually precede C and A-delta in clinical differential block.
